действ. прич. наст. вр. от успокаивать

examples.text: Батюшка, отпевающий мертвых и успокаивающий живых…

glosses: адъектив. приводящий в состояние покоя, рассеивающий беспокойство, тревогу

examples.text: Другое несомненное условие счастья есть труд, во-первых, любимый и свободный труд, во-вторых, труд физический, дающий аппетит и крепкий, успокаивающий сон.
В этом было и что-то успокаивающее, усыпляющее, тихо и покойно стало на душе у Василия…
И В. Путину пришлось сделать успокаивающее заявление о «недопустимости чрезмерных мер» и о «необходимости защищать Конституцию».
― Ничего страшного, ― сказал Сурен успокаивающим тоном психотерапевта.

glosses: The act of making something calmer or an instance of something becoming calmer.
present participle and gerund of calm
present participle and gerund of soothe
present participle and gerund of sooth
The act by which somebody is soothed.

examples.text: There are moments when the brightest minds prefer the soothings of sympathy to all the brilliance of wit, as he that is in need of repose, selects a bed of feathers, rather than of flints.

If in the Breast tumultuous Joys arise,
Musick her soft, assuasive Voice applies;
Or when the Soul is press’d with Cares
Exalts her in enlivening Airs.
“[…] Perhaps,” said Bounderby, starting with all his might at his so quiet and assuasive father-in-law, “you know where your daughter is at the present time?”
The medicine, whatever it might be, had the merit, rare in doctor’s stuff, of being pleasant to take, assuasive of thirst, and imbued with a hardly perceptible fragrance,
The stuff gagged him but he forced it down. This wasn’t smart but the alcohol had an assuasive effect.
[…] the heat of the sun operates in all its vigour, without an assuasive to mitigate its force.

1817, Richard Yates, The Basis of National Welfare, London: F. C. and J. Rivington et al., § 9, p. 112,
the bland, the courteous, the truly Christian assuasives of friendly attention

1908, Mary Virginia Terhune (as Marion Harland), The Housekeeper’s Week, Indianapolis: Bobbs-Merrill, Chapter 23, p. 312,
Nature, as the laity may know it, is a vast pharmacopœia of assuasives and curatives

glosses: An agent or drug that sedates, having a calming or soothing effect, or inducing sleep.
Of a drug: having the effect of calming a person or animal, or putting them to sleep; sedating, sedative.
Having the effect of making someone or something tranquil; calming, soothing.

examples.text: In a preceding paper I have spoken of an English Sunday in the country, and its tranquilizing effect upon the landscape; but where is its sacred influence more strikingly apparent than in the very heart of that great Babel, London?

glosses: The act of calming a person or animal, or putting them to sleep, using a drug.
The act of making someone or something tranquil.
present participle and gerund of tranquilize
